```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "92%"
)

project_dir <- Sys.getenv("CEMITOOL_PROJECT_DIR", unset = "")
if (!nzchar(project_dir)) {
  project_dir <- normalizePath("../..", winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  project_dir <- normalizePath(project_dir, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
}

samples <- read.delim(
  file.path(project_dir, "data/metadata/samples.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

expr <- readRDS(
  file.path(project_dir, "data/processed/expression_log2rpkm.rds")
)

cem <- readRDS(
  file.path(project_dir, "results/beta10/objects/cemitool.rds")
)

param_file <- file.path(project_dir, "results/beta10/parameters.txt")
parameters <- if (file.exists(param_file)) {
  readLines(param_file)
} else {
  character()
}

param_value <- function(key) {
  hit <- grep(paste0("^", key, "="), parameters, value = TRUE)
  if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  sub(paste0("^", key, "="), "", hit[[1]])
}

n_modules <- CEMiTool::nmodules(cem)
beta <- param_value("beta")
```

# Scope

This report documents the computational analysis of the balanced 54-sample subset of GEO accession **GSE98923** used in the CEMiTool baseline workflow.

The report is intended as an analysis record and potential supplementary document for a scientific manuscript. Large machine-readable matrices are not printed in full in the document; complete files are preserved separately and indexed in the supplementary manifest.

# Experimental design

The analysis contains **`r nrow(samples)` samples**, covering two cultivars, three developmental stages, three years, and three biological replicates per cultivar-stage-year combination.

```{r design-table}
design <- with(samples, table(Cultivar, Stage, Year))
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(design),
  caption = "Sample counts by cultivar, developmental stage, and year."
)
```

# Expression data

The processed matrix used for CEMiTool contains **`r nrow(expr)` genes** and **`r ncol(expr)` samples**.

Expression values were derived from the processed RPKM matrix distributed with GSE98923 and transformed as:

\[
\log_2(\mathrm{RPKM} + 1)
\]

The complete matrices are available under:

- `data/processed/expression_rpkm.tsv`
- `data/processed/expression_log2rpkm.tsv`

# CEMiTool analysis

CEMiTool identified **`r n_modules` modules** in the baseline analysis.

The analysis used Pearson correlation, an unsigned network, a signed TOM, a minimum module size of 30, and a fixed random seed of 1234.

Automatic beta selection did not identify a usable value in the initial baseline run. To reproduce the established 54-sample baseline, the soft-thresholding power was fixed explicitly at **beta = 10** using `set_beta = 10` and `force_beta = FALSE`. This value is specific to the present expression matrix and should be re-evaluated if the sample set, normalization, or filtering changes. The recorded beta for this run is **`r beta`**.

```{r parameters-table}
if (length(parameters) > 0) {
  p <- do.call(
    rbind,
    strsplit(parameters, "=", fixed = TRUE)
  )
  p <- as.data.frame(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(p) <- c("parameter", "value")
  knitr::kable(p, caption = "Recorded analysis parameters.")
}
```

# Exported result tables

The following section provides a compact view of every tabular result exported by CEMiTool. Complete tables remain available as machine-readable files under `results/tables/`.

```{r result-tables, results='asis'}
table_files <- list.files(
  file.path(project_dir, "results/beta10/tables"),
  pattern = "\\.(tsv|csv|txt)$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

read_result_table <- function(path) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(path))

  if (ext == "csv") {
    read.csv(
      path,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    read.delim(
      path,
      sep = "\t",
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
}

if (length(table_files) == 0) {
  cat("No exported result tables were found.\n")
} else {
  for (f in table_files) {
    cat("\n## ", basename(f), "\n\n", sep = "")

    x <- tryCatch(
      read_result_table(f),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )

    if (is.null(x)) {
      cat("The table could not be displayed in the report. See the original file.\n")
      next
    }

    cat(
      "Dimensions: ",
      nrow(x),
      " rows x ",
      ncol(x),
      " columns.\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )

    if (ncol(x) > 12) {
      cat(
        "The in-document preview is omitted because this matrix has ",
        ncol(x),
        " columns. The complete table remains available as a machine-readable file.\n"
      )
      next
    }

    display_n <- min(nrow(x), 40)

    print(
      knitr::kable(
        utils::head(x, display_n),
        caption = paste0(
          basename(f),
          if (nrow(x) > display_n) {
            paste0(" - first ", display_n, " rows shown")
          } else {
            ""
          }
        )
      )
    )

    if (nrow(x) > display_n) {
      cat(
        "\nThe complete table is provided as a supplementary machine-readable file.\n"
      )
    }
  }
}
```

# Post-CEMiTool module statistics

This section is an additional statistical layer performed after construction of the beta-10 CEMiTool network. It is not part of the native CEMiTool report and is not stored inside the CEMiTool object.

```{r post-cemitool-load, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
stats_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results", "module_statistics_beta10")
cmp_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results", "comparisons")
rd <- function(x) read.delim(x, sep="\t", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, check.names=FALSE)
anova <- rd(file.path(stats_dir, "module_factorial_ANOVA_typeIII.tsv"))
inter <- rd(file.path(stats_dir, "significant_cultivar_stage_interactions_FDR05.tsv"))
contr <- rd(file.path(stats_dir, "significant_cabernet_vs_pinot_stage_contrasts_FDR05.tsv"))
contr$Direction <- ifelse(contr$estimate > 0, "Cabernet Sauvignon > Pinot noir", "Cabernet Sauvignon < Pinot noir")
year <- anova[anova$Effect == "Year", , drop=FALSE]
year_sig <- year[!is.na(year$FDR) & year$FDR < 0.05, , drop=FALSE]
wide <- reshape(anova[,c("Module","Effect","FDR")], idvar="Module", timevar="Effect", direction="wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^FDR\\.", "FDR_", names(wide))
wide <- wide[order(wide$Module),,drop=FALSE]
match_file <- file.path(cmp_dir, "best_module_matches_beta7_to_beta10.tsv")
matches <- if (file.exists(match_file)) rd(match_file) else NULL
```

## Network calibration and sensitivity

Beta 10 is the primary network and beta 7 is retained as a sensitivity analysis. Module labels are arbitrary across runs, so robustness is evaluated using shared genes rather than matching labels by name.

```{r beta-robustness, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(matches)) {
  keep <- intersect(c("Module_beta7","Module_beta10","Shared_genes","Jaccard","Percent_beta7_retained"), names(matches))
  x <- matches[,keep,drop=FALSE]
  if ("Jaccard" %in% names(x)) x$Jaccard <- round(x$Jaccard,3)
  if ("Percent_beta7_retained" %in% names(x)) x$Percent_beta7_retained <- round(x$Percent_beta7_retained,1)
  print(knitr::kable(x, caption="Best beta7-to-beta10 matches based on gene membership."))
} else cat("Beta7-vs-beta10 comparison table was not available at render time.\n")
```

## Module eigengene model

For each beta-10 biological module, PC1 of standardized module-gene expression was used as the module eigengene. PC1 sign was oriented to correlate positively with mean module expression.

Model:

```text
Eigengene ~ Cultivar * Stage + Year
```

Type III ANOVA used sum-to-zero contrasts and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.

## FDR overview by module

```{r fdr-overview, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (nm in names(wide)[vapply(wide,is.numeric,logical(1))]) wide[[nm]] <- signif(wide[[nm]],4)
print(knitr::kable(wide, caption="FDR by module and model effect."))
```

## Significant Cultivar x Stage interactions

```{r interaction-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (nrow(inter)==0) {
  cat("No module passed FDR < 0.05 for Cultivar x Stage.\n")
} else {
  s <- inter[which.min(inter$FDR),,drop=FALSE]
  cat(paste0("**",nrow(inter)," of ",length(unique(anova$Module))," modules** passed FDR < 0.05. Strongest: **",s$Module,"** (FDR=",format(s$FDR,scientific=TRUE,digits=3),").\n\n"))
  x <- inter
  x$p_value <- format(x$p_value, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  x$FDR <- format(x$FDR, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  keep <- intersect(c("Module","F value","p_value","FDR"), names(x))
  print(knitr::kable(x[,keep,drop=FALSE], caption="Significant Cultivar x Stage interactions."))
}
```

A significant interaction means that the Cabernet-versus-Pinot difference changes with developmental stage. It does not by itself demonstrate a causal relationship with skin thickness.

## Cabernet Sauvignon vs Pinot noir within stage

The contrast is Cabernet Sauvignon minus Pinot noir. Negative estimates therefore indicate a lower module eigengene in Cabernet Sauvignon.

```{r stage-contrasts, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (nrow(contr)==0) {
  cat("No stage-specific contrast passed global FDR < 0.05.\n")
} else {
  x <- contr
  x$estimate <- round(x$estimate,3)
  x$p.value <- format(x$p.value, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  x$FDR_global <- format(x$FDR_global, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  keep <- intersect(c("Module","Stage","estimate","Direction","p.value","FDR_global"), names(x))
  print(knitr::kable(x[,keep,drop=FALSE], caption="Significant cultivar contrasts within stage."))
}
```

## Year effect

```{r year-effect, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(paste0("Year passed FDR < 0.05 in **",nrow(year_sig)," of ",nrow(year)," modules**.\n\n"))
if (nrow(year_sig)) {
  x <- year_sig[,c("Module","p_value","FDR"),drop=FALSE]
  x$p_value <- format(x$p_value, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  x$FDR <- format(x$FDR, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
  print(knitr::kable(x, caption="Modules with significant Year effect."))
}
```

This supports keeping 2012, 2013 and 2014 explicit. The completed robustness layer below tests whether the Cultivar x Stage pattern is stable across years.

## Interpretation boundaries

- GSE98923 is berry pericarp, not isolated skin.
- There is no direct skin-thickness phenotype in this dataset.
- Only two cultivars are compared.
- Several modules have a significant Year effect.
- The baseline uses the historical GEO RPKM matrix.

The subsequent layers use `Eigengene ~ Cultivar * Stage * Year`, functional annotation, hub prioritization, skin-only external comparison and modern raw-read reprocessing. They remain observational and do not convert module association into phenotype causality.

# Integrated evidence from T-004 through T-008

This section connects the vintage, functional, candidate-gene, external-validation and modern-processing layers. Each statement is derived from the canonical machine-readable files loaded below. The historical beta-10 network remains unchanged.

```{r t009-load, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rdp <- function(...) read.delim(file.path(project_dir, ...), sep="\t", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, check.names=FALSE)
year_class <- rdp("results", "year_robustness_beta10", "priority_module_classification.tsv")
year_consistency <- rdp("results", "year_robustness_beta10", "stage_year_consistency.tsv")
mapman_hits <- rdp("results", "functional_enrichment_beta10", "v3_mapman_global_FDR05_hits.tsv")
go_qc <- rdp("results", "go_ora_beta10", "go_annotation_and_test_qc.tsv")
go_hits <- rdp("results", "go_ora_beta10", "go_global_FDR05_hits.tsv")
m5_hubs <- rdp("results", "hub_prioritization_beta10", "m5_focus_genes.tsv")
m10_m2_hubs <- rdp("results", "hub_prioritization_beta10", "m10_m2_focus_genes.tsv")
external_hubs <- rdp("results", "external_skin_validation_beta10", "primary_external_condition_hubs.tsv")
modern_qc <- rdp("results", "fastq_reprocessing_t008", "modern_matrix_qc.tsv")
preservation <- rdp("results", "fastq_reprocessing_t008", "modern_preservation", "module_preservation_summary.tsv")
priority <- c("M5", "M10", "M2", "M3", "M1")
```

## T-004: robustness across vintages

The full model was `Eigengene ~ Cultivar * Stage * Year`. M10 met the prespecified module-level reproducibility rule. M5, M2, M3 and M1 were year-dependent under at least one criterion, but M5 Harvest and M2 Veraison/Harvest retained the same Cabernet-minus-Pinot direction and passed global FDR in all three years. M3 Harvest was dominated in magnitude by 2013, and M1 was not established as stable.

```{r t009-year-table}
x <- year_class[match(priority, year_class$Module), c("Module", "Classification", "Stages_with_2plus_year_FDR_hits", "Single_year_dominant_stages", "Detected_direction_reversal")]
names(x) <- c("Module", "Classification", "Repeated stage", "Single-year dominant", "Sign reversal")
knitr::kable(x, caption="Vintage-robustness classification of the five interaction modules.")
```

```{r t009-m5-profile, fig.cap="M5 observed eigengene means and biological-replicate standard errors by stage, cultivar and year. Inferential contrasts come from the full factorial model."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(project_dir, "results", "year_robustness_beta10", "profiles", "M5_stage_by_year.png"))
```

## T-005 and T-005A: functional enrichment and ontology audit

MapMan v3 was the primary annotation layer because it covered 2,608 of 3,050 beta-10 genes. M5 was globally enriched for phenolic/stilbenoid and PAL categories. Newer v5.1 labels assigned several of the same chromosome-16 genes to CHS/flavonoid categories, so the exact CHS-versus-STS identity remains unresolved.

The official 2026-07-26 Gene Ontology audit identified 390 obsolete IDs among 3,556 represented Grapedia terms. After filtering, the annotated background remained 519 genes and all six global-FDR GO hits occurred in M9. Sparse coverage prevents treating the absence of GO hits in M5, M10, M2, M3 or M1 as biological absence.

```{r t009-mapman-table}
x <- mapman_hits[mapman_hits$Module == "M5", c("TermID", "TermName", "Overlap_k", "Fold_enrichment", "FDR_global_module_terms")]
x <- head(x[order(x$FDR_global_module_terms), ], 7)
x$TermName <- c(
  "Stilbenoid biosynthesis", "Phenolics", "Secondary metabolism",
  "PAL", "PAL activity", "p-coumaroyl-CoA biosynthesis",
  "p-coumaroyl-CoA biosynthesis"
)[seq_len(nrow(x))]
x$Fold_enrichment <- round(x$Fold_enrichment, 2)
x$FDR_global_module_terms <- format(x$FDR_global_module_terms, scientific=TRUE, digits=3)
names(x) <- c("Term", "MapMan category", "Hits", "Fold", "Global FDR")
knitr::kable(x, caption="Leading globally significant MapMan v3 terms in M5.")
```

## T-006: hub-gene prioritization

Intramodular connectivity was calculated on the frozen beta-10 adjacency. Eight of the 11 M5 top-decile hubs belong to the chromosome-16 family with conflicting STS/CHS labels. A copper amine oxidase candidate ranked fifth and a NAC-domain transcription-factor candidate ranked seventh; PAL genes were enriched at module level but were not in the top 11. M10 prioritized a bHLH candidate and a HAK/KUP/KT transporter. M2 prioritized MYB- and FAR1-labeled candidates, while recurrent exact zeros require mapping- and structure-aware interpretation.

```{r t009-m5-hubs}
x <- m5_hubs[m5_hubs$Top_decile_kWithin, c("Gene", "Rank_kWithin", "kWithin", "V3_stilbenoid_label", "V5_CHS_label", "V3_NAC_label", "Harvest_same_direction_all_years")]
x$kWithin <- round(x$kWithin, 2)
x$Evidence <- paste0(
  ifelse(x$V3_stilbenoid_label, "v3-STS ", ""),
  ifelse(x$V5_CHS_label, "v5-CHS ", ""),
  ifelse(x$V3_NAC_label, "NAC", "")
)
x <- x[, c("Gene", "Rank_kWithin", "kWithin", "Evidence")]
names(x) <- c("Gene", "Rank", "kWithin", "Annotation evidence")
knitr::kable(x, caption="M5 top-decile intramodular hubs and selected annotation evidence.")
```

## T-007: external skin-only expression support

GSE72421 and PRJNA260535 were analyzed as independent skin-only evidence, not as additional GSE98923 replicates. In GSE72421 well-watered skin, 11 of 11 evaluable M5 hubs passed BH correction within the predefined 37-hub set and matched the stable Harvest direction. In PRJNA260535 at 24 degrees Brix, four of seven evaluable M5 hubs passed. CuAO- and NAC-labeled M5 candidates agreed in both sources. M10 support was limited, whereas selected M2 MYB and FAR1 candidates agreed but had incomplete RNA-seq coverage.

```{r t009-external-summary}
x <- aggregate(cbind(Assayed=external_hubs$Assayed, Significant=!is.na(external_hubs$BH_prespecified_top37) & external_hubs$BH_prespecified_top37 < 0.05) ~ Dataset + Condition + Module, data=external_hubs, FUN=sum)
x <- x[x$Dataset %in% c("GSE72421", "PRJNA260535"), ]
knitr::kable(x, caption="Evaluable and BH-supported predefined hubs in the two primary external comparisons.")
```

## T-008: modern raw-read processing and module preservation

All 54 FASTQ and Salmon outputs passed integrity and quantification checks. The modern matrix contains 47,971 genes and 54 samples. Preservation used only 1,922 audited reciprocal one-to-one legacy-to-v5.1 mappings and fixed historical memberships.

```{r t009-preservation-table}
x <- preservation[match(c("M1", "M5", "M10", "M2", "M3"), preservation$Module), c("Module", "Total_beta10_genes", "Mapped_genes", "Mapped_fraction", "Modern_vs_canonical_full_PC1_Pearson", "Adjacency_beta10_Spearman", "Zsummary_preservation", "Preservation_class")]
x$Mapped_fraction <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100*x$Mapped_fraction)
x$Modern_vs_canonical_full_PC1_Pearson <- round(x$Modern_vs_canonical_full_PC1_Pearson, 3)
x$Adjacency_beta10_Spearman <- round(x$Adjacency_beta10_Spearman, 3)
x$Zsummary_preservation <- round(x$Zsummary_preservation, 2)
names(x) <- c("Module", "Genes", "Mapped", "Coverage", "Eigengene r", "Adjacency rho", "Zsummary", "Class")
knitr::kable(x, caption="Fixed-membership preservation against modern read reprocessing.")
```

```{r t009-preservation-figure, fig.cap="WGCNA module-preservation Zsummary statistics. Coverage and mapping ambiguity must be considered together with Zsummary."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(project_dir, "results", "fastq_reprocessing_t008", "modern_preservation", "module_preservation_zsummary.png"))
```

M1 was strongly preserved. M5, M10 and M2 showed moderate preservation of their mapped cores with eigengene correlations of 0.986--0.998. M2 mapped only 81 of 214 genes, so the complete module is not declared preserved. M3 preservation was not supported.

# Integrated interpretation

M5 has the strongest convergent evidence: the largest cultivar-by-stage interaction, a repeated Harvest direction across vintages, coherent phenolic-pathway enrichment, externally supported hubs and moderate mapped-core preservation after modern reprocessing. M10 has the strongest module-level vintage reproducibility but less functional and external support. M2 retains repeated Veraison and Harvest contrasts and a preserved mapped core, but limited mapping coverage and exact-zero patterns require structural and reference-aware follow-up. M3 and M1 remain lower-confidence biological priorities despite specific statistical or technical signals.

# Final limitations

- The primary material is berry pericarp, not isolated skin.
- No analyzed dataset measures berry skin thickness.
- Cultivar is entangled with clone, rootstock and planting history in the original field system.
- External sources differ in year, condition, developmental definition and platform.
- MapMan and GO coverage are incomplete, and duplicated CHS/STS-family genes remain ambiguous.
- Reciprocal one-to-one mapping excludes ambiguous genes and therefore underrepresents some families.
- Coexpression, enrichment, hub status, external concordance and preservation are not causal evidence.

# Final conclusion

The project supports cultivar-associated developmental transcriptional programs in grape berry pericarp. M5 is the leading integrated candidate program, M10 is the clearest year-reproducible module, and M2 warrants mapping- and structure-aware follow-up. No current result demonstrates that a module or gene causes thick or thin berry skin.

<!-- END T009_INTEGRATED_EVIDENCE -->
